My own oracle check (own_oracle.py with lie_games roots, mutate, gram, kostant_play and the golden types and kostant keys; 0 failures): (a) On all 32 boards, the root of largest form value at which no mutation raises any city is types.highest_root, and it lies above every root. (b) With single roads (A, D, E, 16 boards) it is the only such root. (c) With a double or triple road (B2-B8, C2-C8, F4, G2) there is exactly one other, highest_short_root. It has the smaller form value, it is short, and it lies above every short root. (d) Kostant's game from every simple root population ends at the highest root from a long node and at the highest short root from a short node. I checked lowest-first, highest-first and 5 random choice orders, and the ends equal kostant.end_from_node. (e) With single roads, the raising moves among positive roots are exactly the root-poset covers, each adding one Martian. With a double or triple road they are not: the largest rise is 2 on B, C and F4 and 3 on G2, and every rise above 1 passes over the positive root p+alpha_i. Adoption: the tests check the finding's expected computationally on all 32 boards (SPEC 2.6 rule, F13, T2/2.16) and match the new wording. Only the old-text assertions and the counterexample assertions were replaced, the latter by the observed values. Every computation is kept.

On the fixed build (4002 links, 0 problems) it prints the new definition: '... the root population of largest form value at which no mutation raises any city. ... exactly one other, of smaller form value: the highest short root. Kostant's game, attributed to Kostant, ends there ...'. It still prints 16 of 32 and exits 1, because its exit condition is only that the definition contains 'no mutation raises any city', and the new definition keeps that phrase. The behaviour the finding describes, a rule that names two roots, is gone: the rule now selects by largest form value, which picks exactly the highest root on all 32 boards (my oracle, above), and the entry names the other root. The regression is the same test as P6-RT-09-01 (separate '// regression: P6-RT-13-01'). Its loop over the 32 golden types fails under the scratch revert with the '16 of 32 boards' message above and passes after restore.

The original reproducer fails on the branch at line 104, toContain('Its shape depends only on which nodes are ringed'): the text is gone. With only that line dropped, the test passes: its last assertion, /shape depends only on which nodes are ringed/ is false, holds, and the squared lengths are [[2,4],[2,16]]. python3 redteam-RT-09-p6-wythoff.py reference printed f-vector [24,36,14,1] for both (0,1,1) and (0,2,1), with squared lengths {2,4} (ratio 2) and {2,16} (ratio 8). The fixer's content-glossary-wythoff.test.ts ('// regression: P6-RT-09-03') passes. Under the scratch revert it fails at line 42: '... Its shape depends only on which nodes are ringed (, ). On B3 the orbits of (0,1,1) and (0,2,1) ring the same nodes and have the same face counts (24, 36, 14) but squared edge lengths 2 and 4 against 2 and 16 ...: expected true to be false'. My oracle checked 8 pairs with the same ringed nodes (B3 (0,1,1)/(0,2,1), A2 (1,1)/(1,2), A3, B3 (1,1,1)/(1,3,2), C3, G2, D4, F4). In each pair the f-vectors are equal, and the map w.lambda -> w.lambda' (by words) is a bijection of vertices that sends edges onto edges. The edge-length ratios differ (2 vs 8, 1 vs 4, 2 vs 9, 3 vs 4/3, ...), and every squared length is 2 d_i a_i^2. So the faces are fixed by which nodes are ringed and the lengths are not, as the new row says. The cited claim keeps Cite Cox35 and CKPS95.
